revision_summary: Two quote/reference issues need fixing on rerun: (1) In cherry_pick_moments[1] (05:10), the claim that the usage number 4147 was 'already given by customer at 01:38-ish' is factually wrong — the number 4147 actually appears at 05:43, AFTER the 05:10 ask. This undercuts the entire coaching point ('rep should have accepted the number immediately') since the number wasn't on the table yet. Correct the timeline: the rep's repeated graph-asks at 05:10 and 06:26 happen BEFORE the usage figure is volunteered at 05:43-ish, so the 'slow pivot' framing should shift to note the rep asks twice, THEN receives the usable number, THEN a third confirming exchange follows — not that the rep ignored an already-supplied number. (2) Fix the mislabeled classification 'curiosity_creation_failure' used twice (05:10, 06:26) — this schema concept (coaching_philosophy.curiosity_over_features) is about not over-explaining solar features to customers, unrelated to bill-format friction. Relabel these as a tech/bill-friction classification tied to bill_collection.alternative_paths, and explicitly invoke the schema's 2-minute pivot time budget (bill_collection.alternative_paths.elderly_low_tech_protocol / landline_protocol) since the friction window here runs roughly 5+ minutes (02:44–07:44), a stronger and directly schema-grounded coaching hook than what was used. (3) Remove or correct the invented protocol references 'protocols (general handshake discipline)' and 'protocols (ownership of follow-up)' in the unanchored_soft_exit entries — no such named protocols exist in the schema; either drop the schema_reference field or mark it null/TBD rather than fabricating a plausible-sounding citation. (4) Consider consolidating the two near-duplicate unanchored_soft_exit entries (09:52 and 10:13) into one moment to avoid inflating the moment count. (5) Add the 08:44 'Okay. I think I think this is fine' hedge and the 00:42 ambiguous phone-vs-in-person appointment-type moment as additional cherry_pick_moments — both are concrete, quotable, schema-relevant gaps currently underrepresented in the output.
